content.title: About
content.content: Sparkling wine is a fermented beverage made from grapes that contains natural or added carbon dioxide, creating characteristic bubbles. It can be dry, off‑dry, or sweet, and varies by region of production and grape varieties used.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first sparkling wine was produced in the Champagne region of France in the 17th century.
The traditional method (méthode champenoise) requires a secondary fermentation in the bottle, giving finer and more persistent bubbles.
More than 30 grape varieties are used for sparkling wine, including Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, and Pinot Meunier.
Sparkling wine is typically served chilled at 6–8 °C to highlight its aroma and freshness.
In many countries the term “Champagne” is reserved for sparkling wine produced in the Champagne region.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds in wine help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Moderate consumption may improve lipid profiles and reduce the risk of heart disease.

items.title: Rich in polyphenols
items.content: Polyphenols promote microcirculation and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Acidity and gentle carbonation can stimulate gastric juice production.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of B1, B2 and B6 contribute to energy metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to intoxication, liver problems, and other health issues.

items.title: Sugar levels
items.content: Sweeter styles may raise blood glucose, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of sedatives and anticoagulants.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit or avoid alcohol consumption.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach in individuals with gastritis or ulcer disease.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: Serve sparkling wine in flutes or tulip glasses to preserve bubbles. It can be enjoyed as an aperitif, paired with seafood, light appetizers, cheeses, and fruit desserts. For cocktails, mix champagne with juices or liqueurs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place on its side to keep the cork moist. After opening, seal with a proper stopper and consume within 1–3 days.
